artifact_png_review.method: Decoded every retained PNG at 1280x720 with Pillow and hashed its unchanged bytes; the full 2920-frame PNG set was checked on the runner and is not included in the selected artifact

review_scope: Static comparison of extracted video frames and original selected PNGs, paired with exported World contact clocks. Does not claim human playback review, audio review or physical-device playtest.

accepted: All four defenders show articulated body compression and recovery across their eight profiles; the animation is not limited to a tint or rigid transform.
Standing/crouching guards, airborne reaction, grounded fall and rise have distinct body poses. Grounded uncaptured observations retain physical floor support.
The barrage restarts Head at each of its eight contacts and samples all four drawings during each nine-frame response in every captured direction/damage condition.
limits: At the apex of throws, the HUD overlaps parts of the defender; the body stays within the captured frame but is not fully unobstructed.
The shared standing-guard pose of Go raises its arms above the head while this captured body punch contacts the lower abdomen, leaving visible separation from the BLOCK effect.
In the first recoil drawing of Duke during the C++ barrage, the spark is visibly offset from the head; the fingertips approach the top of the nose.
Go shows some muzzle/face-volume variation between the first two recovery drawings.

Video is continuous only for the primary direction with damage enabled. Other direction/damage conditions have original PNG samples and full state reports; these do not establish human-perceived fluency.

visual_review.method: Agent image-tool inspection of side-by-side extracted video drawings and original PNG selections; the contact sheets used only scaling/labels for comparison
